Subject: Index routing: technical FAQ + SLA alignment (S3 / pgvector / Pinecone)

Sam —

Thanks again for walking through the integration patterns yesterday. As discussed, we've put together a short technical FAQ to capture the routing expectations when customers use the AtlasData index layer in front of pgvector/S3-backed indices and fallthrough to Pinecone for high-speed lookups. Goal: a single doc we can both reference in the partner portal and send to customers when scoping hybrid storage.

Attached: index-routing-faq-draft.pdf (draft) and a simple latency matrix (routing-latency-matrix.xlsx).

Top asks from our side:
- Can AtlasData confirm the heartbeat/healthcheck semantics you expect for cold-index read routing? Specifically: TTL for warm shard affinity, recommended probe interval, and backoff policy.
- What are the guaranteed consistency semantics if a write is routed to S3-first then asynchronously indexed to pgvector? (Eventual, read-after-write window)
- Any constraints on index shard placement we should document (e.g., affinity to a region for residency / compliance)

If you can annotate the attached PDF with quick notes, we can incorporate them and publish. I propose a 30-min sync Wed 5/20 to finalize. Ben/Vanessa — FYI please review the draft and flag any commercial asks we should include (SLA tiers, support handoff).

Best,
Laura

On Sun, May 17, 2026 at 09:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sam —
> 
> Thanks again for walking through the integration patterns yesterday...

Laura — thanks for the summary and the draft. Quick answers inline and a few open items:

1) Heartbeat / healthcheck: AtlasData recommends a 30s probe by default, with a 3x miss window before evicting a shard from hot routing. Customers with tighter SLAs can reduce probe to 10s, but we see increased false-positives on spotty networks. We'll add an optional config knob: "probe_interval_seconds" and "eviction_threshold" in the draft.

2) Write consistency: the default behavior is write-through to S3 (durable), and an async job pushes vectors into pgvector within the same region. Our typical read-after-write window is 60-120s depending on batch backfill cadence; we can provide a synchronous indexing option for customers that need <5s R/A/W at a premium. We'll mark these two paths in the FAQ.

3) Shard placement: we support region affinity tags on index creation. For compliance use-cases we'll include guidance for pinning to a region and exposing residency as a property in the index metadata.

Open items for Redwood:
- What SLA tiers should we advertise jointly? Basic / Standard / Premium? If so, do you have a baseline latency SLA for the Premium lane (e.g., p95 < 150ms) when Pinecone hot reads are used?
- Error handling: how should we present retry vs fallback semantics when pgvector is slow and fallthrough to Pinecone is used? We can add suggested retry windows and circuit-breaker defaults.

I'll annotate the PDF with these points and return before Tuesday. Wed 5/20 10:00 PT works for a 30-min finalize unless you prefer morning.

—Sam
Head of Integrations
AtlasData

Thanks — reviewed the draft and Sam's notes. Two quick commercial / ops asks to add to the FAQ before we share externally:

- Support boundaries: define on-call ownership by error class (indexing failures vs routing failures). Example: AtlasData handles index-tier availability; Redwood owns inference routing degradations that originate in our serving runtime. Put a one-line callout with pager contacts and escalation matrix link.

- Cost/chargeback guidance: add a short table showing expected token-per-lookup cost delta when fallthrough to Pinecone occurs vs staying on regional pgvector. This helps customers estimate egress and search costs. I've added a sample row in routing-latency-matrix.xlsx under "cost-estimates".

I'll join the Wed sync. Also suggest we lock down the Premium latency target now so AtlasData can validate through their perf harness. If we aim for p95 < 150ms on hot-path (pinecone), we can comfortably map Standard to p95 < 350ms and Basic as best-effort.

-bc
